reasons.text: Energy charges do not match units x tariff on 100% of bills (worst bill charged 12% of expected)
64% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
52% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.82x the cost floor)
74% of high-value consignments have no e-way bill
89% of product sales go to buyers incorporated under a year before the invoice

inspection_checklist: Verify the electricity bills directly with the DISCOM (units, tariff, amount); the uploaded copies do not reconcile.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
